persistence_invariants.brief: A composite UNIQUE constraint on (sku, location) rejects a second row for the same pair at the DB level (R3).
sku is NOT NULL; an insert without a sku is rejected by the schema.
location is NOT NULL; an insert without a location is rejected by the schema.
quantity is NOT NULL; an insert without a quantity is rejected by the schema.
A CHECK (quantity >= 0) constraint rejects a negative quantity at the DB level (R2); quantity is an INTEGER column so fractional values cannot be stored.

After downgrading the initial create_table migration to its own down_revision and running upgrade head, stock_records and its columns, unique(sku, location) and CHECK constraint are present again (schema recreated; no data-survival claim for an initial create).

access_patterns.brief: Full list of stock_records ORDER BY location, sku for the home stock-by-location table; the (sku, location) unique index is sku-leading and does not serve a location-leading sort.

api_contracts.item: Request JSON {sku: string, location: string, quantity: integer >= 0, tracking_code: string|null}. 201 body: the created record {id: int, sku: string, location: string, quantity: int, tracking_code: string|null}. 422 body: {errors: {<field>: <field-named message>}} keyed by sku|location|quantity. 409 body: {error: 'A record for that SKU at that location already exists'}.
Bare JSON array (no envelope), ordered by location then sku; each item {id: int, sku: string, location: string, quantity: int, tracking_code: string|null}. Empty array when no records exist.

Single record object for the exact (sku, location) key: {id: int, sku: string, location: string, quantity: int, tracking_code: string|null, par_level: int|null}. par_level is always null in F1 (no par-level storage until a later feature). 404 body {error: 'Stock record not found'} when no row matches.

nfrs.fitness_function: Downgrade the stock_records create migration to its down_revision, then upgrade head; the table and its constraints are recreated on the paired branch.
nfrs.requirement: F1 creates the initial stock_records table; no prior data exists and no adjustments exist in F1 (audit trail arrives with F2). The initial migration must be reversible so later additive migrations build on a proven baseline.

nfrs.fitness_function: POSTing quantity -3 returns 422 keyed on quantity and a direct insert of quantity -1 is rejected by the CHECK constraint on the paired branch.
nfrs.requirement: A filed stock record never holds a negative quantity; rejected at write time by the service and the DB CHECK. Overcommit is N/A in F1 (no pick/allocation operation exists until F4).

nfrs.fitness_function: Filing an existing (sku, location) returns 409 and exactly one row with the original quantity remains on the paired branch.
nfrs.requirement: Each (sku, location) is uniquely addressable; a duplicate filing is refused at write time with an inline message (409), never a second row, never an error page.

nfrs.fitness_function: The test session's engine URL resolves to the paired Lakebase branch (not sqlite/in-memory) and the alembic head is applied before tests run.
nfrs.requirement: Integration and DB tests run against the paired Lakebase branch via DATABASE_URL; no mock or in-memory DB.

nfrs.fitness_function: Submitting the stock-record form updates the page in place with no document navigation (Playwright asserts no full reload) and the endpoint responds application/json.
nfrs.requirement: The UI is the React SPA under client/; the boundary returns JSON only and form submits are async with no full-page reload.
N/A for F1 - no barcode-scan interaction exists until F8; recorded for traceability.
nfrs.fitness_function: N/A – no operation in F1 exercises this; defended by the feature that introduces it (scan F8 / search F9).
A submission missing sku returns 422 with errors.sku naming the SKU field, and the client renders it in stock-record-sku-error.
nfrs.requirement: Validation failures name the offending field and render inline next to it; never a generic 'bad request'.

nfrs.fitness_function: The parent-aware schema diff on the paired branch shows only additions (the stock_records table) for F1.
nfrs.requirement: F1's migration is a purely additive create_table; nothing existing is altered or dropped.

nfrs.fitness_function: A record filed with a blank tracking code is stored with tracking_code IS NULL on the paired branch.
nfrs.requirement: An absent tracking code is stored as NULL (S1) so readers (S2 list, S3 detail) render an explicit 'not tracked'; each optional field (tracking code, par level) is judged independently; empty location state is owned by S2.
N/A for F1 - search/filter is explicitly out of scope (F9); recorded for traceability.
nfrs.fitness_function: N/A – no operation in F1 exercises this; defended by the feature that introduces it (scan F8 / search F9).

open_decisions.question: Re-filing an existing (sku, location): refuse or update in place?
open_decisions.resolution: Refuse with 409 + inline message; quantity changes are adjustments (F2). Consistent with AC5 and R3.

open_decisions.question: Is the tracking code required?
open_decisions.resolution: Optional; blank is stored as NULL so readers render 'not tracked'.

open_decisions.question: The IA lists optional Batch/Serial inputs on the form; F1 carries batch/serial inside the tracking code (spec Q4). Should the F1 form omit them until F6?
Where does a record's par level come from in F1, given stock_records has no par-level column?
open_decisions.resolution: F1 stores no par level; the EP3 detail contract returns par_level: null (rendered 'not tracked'). A later par-level feature adds a nullable column additively. Consistent with S2's par-level column showing 'not tracked'; no sibling AC contradicted.
